title: HackCodex 2026: 36-Hour National Hackathon
description: Our flagship annual national hackathon bringing together over 600+ collegiate builders to build high-impact solutions across AI, Web3, ClimateTech, and Spatial Computing.
fullDescription: HackCodex 2026 is the culmination of university tech innovation. Over 36 non-stop hours, teams from top engineering institutions across the country compete for $15,000+ in cash prizes, API credits, and direct venture incubator interviews. Includes 6 expert mentorship roundtables, midnight pizza sprints, and live keynote firesides.
highlights: 25+ Industry Mentors from Tier 1 Tech Firms
Fast-track internship interviews with sponsor partners

title: WebGL & Three.js Shader Masterclass
description: An intensive hands-on workshop taking students from foundational 3D coordinate mathematics to writing custom GLSL vertex and fragment shaders in React Three Fiber.
fullDescription: Step into the world of creative coding and GPU acceleration. Participants will build their own interactive 3D particle constellation, learn post-processing bloom pipelines, and optimize frame rendering for consumer mobile devices. All assets and code starter templates provided.
highlights: Custom Shader Starter Kit to keep

title: Neural Architectures: LLMs & Quantized Edge AI
description: An architectural deep-dive into Transformer attention mechanisms, local 4-bit quantization with llama.cpp, and deploying private models on modest GPU hardware.
fullDescription: Attended by over 320 students and faculty members, this session broke down how modern Large Language Models work beneath the hype. The speaker demonstrated running 7B parameter instruction-tuned models on a standard Apple M2 laptop with real-time streaming output.
highlights: Q&A session covering AI engineering career paths

title: Codex DevFest 2026: Spring Code Sprint
description: A rapid 12-hour high-intensity prototype sprint where 45 student teams built campus utility tools, developer utilities, and interactive web games.
fullDescription: DevFest Spring tested speed, resilience, and product intuition. Teams were given surprise API constraints and had 12 hours to ship a functioning deployment. Top projects included an automated bus tracker and a peer note-sharing markdown platform.

title: System Design: Scaling to 10M Concurrent Users
description: Interactive whiteboard session dissecting horizontal scaling, distributed caching with Redis, database sharding, and fault-tolerant message brokers.
fullDescription: An invaluable session for students preparing for Tier-1 engineering interviews. We mapped out the complete architecture of a global URL shortener, a live streaming chat service, and an e-commerce flash sale queue with zero double-booking.
highlights: Comprehensive System Design PDF Handbook Distributed
